verification.corrected_summary: The author cites a folk aphorism — 「如果想油價跌，那現在油價一定不能跌」 (if you want oil prices to fall, oil must first not fall) — which he explicitly flags as borrowed and merely directional (「不知道誰說的，但道理是相通的」), NOT a stated 'supply is extremely inelastic' thesis. His OPEC remark 「一直拒絕擴產的opec，一直支持俄羅斯的opec+秘書長」 is a sardonic one-liner occasioned by the OPEC+ secretary-general's death, observing that OPEC has refused to expand output — an aside, not a developed forecast of sustained high prices. He quotes China's 《石油价格管理办法》第六条 refined-oil pricing band: below $40/bbl, refined-product prices are computed at $40 with normal processing margin; $40–80 normal processing margin; above $80 the processing margin is progressively deducted down to zero; above $130 retail gasoline/diesel prices are in principle not raised (or raised little), with fiscal measures protecting supply — so very high crude squeezes downstream refiners (Sinopec/PetroChina-type names). Note this mechanism is the author QUOTING regulation (prefaced only 「對誰影響大？」), not his own original analysis. Consistent with it, his one-character reply '85' (correcting a commenter's '$90') implies ~$85 crude is most favorable for petrochem/refiner names — a single character, not a developed view. Critically, his own stated optimum is that oil prices stay FLAT for three to five years (「油價不漲不跌三五年，應該是最理想」), voiced while he was short both CNOOC puts and calls — i.e. he favors moderate, stable crude (good for his option-income positions and for refiners), not ever-higher OPEC-restraint-driven prices. Evidence is thin (a few offhand remarks plus a quoted regulation), not a developed macro framework.
issues: INTERPRETIVE GLOSS: 'Oil supply is extremely inelastic' appears nowhere in the corpus. In post 225154031 the author explicitly flags 「如果想油價跌，那現在油價一定不能跌」 as a borrowed saying (「不知道誰說的，但道理是相通的」), echoing a third-party aphorism that sits in the //@郭荆璞 repost span (「从石头里榨出油比从人头里榨出血来要难的多」 — not the author's words). Recasting this as a structural supply-elasticity thesis over-reads the source.

OVER-ELEVATION + MISREAD OCCASION: post 224658994's one-liner 「一直拒絕擴產的opec，一直支持俄羅斯的opec+秘書長。」 (2022-07-07) was occasioned by the OPEC+ secretary-general Barkindo's death — the thread (c248036752 「尽管巴尔金多…终究也只是个棋子」, c248034188 「下一任是亲美的科威特海瑟姆.盖斯」, c248026285/c248042151 CIA speculation) shows it is a sardonic epitaph insinuating the death was linked to his anti-expansion, pro-Russia stance. The card promotes this aside into 'a structural reason to expect supportive prices' — a developed bullish thesis the author never states.

OMITTED CONTRADICTING VIEW (most serious): at post 224024550 the author states his actual optimum: 「油價不漲不跌三五年，應該是最理想，家最符合我的利益」 (flat oil for 3-5 years is most ideal / most aligned with my interests). The nested author reply c247048392 shows the context: he was short BOTH a CNOOC put and call (「你說不死不活，我是不是應該很開心」), so the preference is moderate, STABLE crude — partly an option-seller's low-volatility interest — not OPEC-restraint-driven high prices. The card leads with a bullish supply-restraint framing and buries the optimum, inverting the author's emphasis.

UNDER-CITED SUBPRINCIPLE: '~$85 crude is most favorable for downstream refiners' rests entirely on the one-character author reply 「85」 (comment c244944256 in post 222544728), a terse correction to commenter c244942196's 「不超过90每桶 对石化最有利」; the follow-up c244949180 (「不超过85，好的」) only confirms how readers parsed it. That comment is not among the citation_seeds, so the subprinciple lacks cited support and is extremely thin.

ATTRIBUTION NUANCE: the price-band mechanism (> $80 progressive deduction of processing margin to zero; > $130 prices 「原则上不提或少提」 with fiscal measures) is the author QUOTING 《石油价格管理办法》第六条 in post 222544728 (prefaced only 「對誰影響大？」); the card presents the mechanism as the author's own analysis rather than a quoted regulation.

OVERSTATED evidence_strength: declared 'strong', but the macro thesis rests on a borrowed aphorism, a sardonic one-liner occasioned by a death, a quoted government regulation, and a one-character reply; the corpus's bulk oil content is CNOOC equity-level profit sensitivity, not a structured macro view. 'weak'/'moderate' is honest.
verification.new_context_notes: All three cited posts (225154031, 224658994, 222544728) gained ZERO new comment ids in the refresh, so seed verification and thread readings are unchanged. Re-checking the contradicting-view post 224024550 against the refreshed corpus_complete.md: (a) the post body verbatim is 「油價不漲不跌三五年，應該是最理想，家最符合我的利益」 — the original verdict's quotation dropped the stray 「家」; (b) the nested author reply c247048392 (nested under @郭荆璞's top-level comment, so plausibly newly captured by the full-nesting crawl) reveals he voiced the flat-price preference while short both a CNOOC put and call (「你說不死不活，我是不是應該很開心」), tying the preference to his short-strangle option-income positioning. This refines, and if anything strengthens, the original omitted-contradicting-view issue; nothing in the fuller context resolves any original issue, so the verdict stays overgeneralized.

card_title_en: EV-penetration ceiling and treating unenacted policy as non-information

Discount announced-but-not-enacted policy (EU 2035 ban) until it actually passes — but mark your sector thesis to evidence (he admits his anti-EV view 'seems wrong').
